brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.

requirements.evidence: 7 full bases: piece:0,0,0 + 6 ring (1,0 / 0,1 / -1,1 / -1,0 / 0,-1 / 1,-1); single body, check_build ok, meshClash clear
3 spikes placed with variant stud + facing down: spike:0#-1,0|-1,1|0,0, spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1, spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0
requirements.requirement: standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet

finish.summary: Built 7-cell honeycomb (center + 6 ring) on 3 down-facing stud spikes as feet; capped open faces, locked joints, check clear.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Building your seven-cell honeycomb on stud-spike feet.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

events.text: Feet confirmed facing down — now I'll seal and verify the build.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.
